summary: Independent review of the 160-row x 44-column SDRF (one TMTpro-16plex set, 16 channels x 10 high-pH fractions) found no blocker or important issues. Channel-to-sample mapping matches the deposited study-design channel table exactly, all 10 RAW files are mapped once per channel, technical metadata matches the RAW headers and the PRIDE protocols, and ontology terms resolve. Only minor improvements remain.

reviewer_context.context: Fresh reviewer subagent without the producer transcript. Read only scratchpad/PXD047503/, the artifact, the evidence manifest and producer report (both treated as untrusted), the spec and installed templates. Did not read reports/superseded or other accessions.

spec_compliance.evidence: I derived the active templates myself as ms-proteomics + human + cell-lines (TMT DDA on human cell lines; affinity-proteomics is for Olink/SomaScan, so it does not apply). Each row has 44 fields with no CR characters or stray whitespace. The (source name, assay name, label) combination is unique and no data file/label pair repeats. Repeated columns (sdrf template x3, dissociation method x2, modification parameters x4) follow the repeated-column rule. The custom columns characteristics[IP replicate], [bait] and [cellular component] are well formed and supported by the sources. The spec (SAMPLE-GUIDELINES) explicitly allows organism part = not applicable for cell lines.

ontology_integrity.evidence: Checked against the offline OLS cache: Ewing sarcoma (MONDO:0012817/EFO:0000174), myxoid liposarcoma (MONDO:0013280/EFO:0000613), nucleus GO:0005634, cell line, male PATO:0000384, Homo sapiens, PRIDE:0000627 DDA, PRIDE:0000564 hpHRP, PRIDE:0000608 DTT, PRIDE:0000605 MMTS, MS:1000133 CID, MS:1000422 beam-type CID, MS:1002732 Orbitrap Fusion Lumos, MS:1001251 Trypsin, PRIDE:0000664 technology type, UNIMOD:2016 TMTpro, UNIMOD:39 Methylthio, UNIMOD:35 Oxidation, and PRIDE label terms TMT126..TMT134N. All labels and accessions match. The cell line names are absent from clo/bto/efo, but the Cellosaurus accessions CVCL_2213 and CVCL_S813 match the RRIDs given in the paper.

source_evidence.evidence: All 16 label-to-sample assignments match the study_design_sample_info channel table (126 = EWS BRG1 R3 ... 134N = EWS BRG1 R2). Baits and the IgG control match the paper's IP section: BRG1-biotin, DDIT3-biotin, FLI1-biotin and Normal mouse IgG-biotin sc-2762 on 50 ug nuclear extract, which supports cellular component = nucleus. The paper says the IPs were done 'in technical replicates', which supports biological replicate = 1. The RAW headers for all 10 files show Orbitrap Lumos, the TMTpro16_MS3_SPS10 method, CID 30% and HCD 55%. The PRIDE protocols give DTT, MMTS, trypsin, TMTpro-16plex, 40 bRP fractions concatenated to 10, 5 ppm / 0.6 Da, and the mods. Cellosaurus fields give male for both lines, 22Y for TC-71 and no age for 402-91. PRIDE's 'acute leukemia' disease entry is wrong and was correctly not used.

file_mapping.evidence: files_compact.json lists exactly 10 RAW files (Lumos_210702_13..22.raw), and all 10 appear in comment[data file], each with 16 channel rows. No non-raw files are referenced. RAW sample names 4231 TMTpro F016..F106 increase with file number, consistent with fraction identifiers 1..10.

design_consistency.evidence: Counts recomputed: 402-91 has BRG1 x3, DDIT3 x3 and IgG x2; TC-71 has BRG1 x3, FLI1 x3 and IgG x2, for 16 channels and 160 rows. The factor values bait and cell line match the characteristics. DDIT3 appears only in 402-91 and FLI1 only in TC-71, which is inherent to the design. One pooled TMT set gives technical replicate 1. The FLI1 IP channels were excluded from analysis in the paper but are present in the data, so annotating them is correct.

omission_safety.evidence: Every non-reserved value traces to PRIDE, the paper, the RAW headers, the design table or the saved Cellosaurus fields. No sample-level value was inferred from a cohort summary. Unknown values use 'not available', except individual and organism part, which use 'not applicable' (see minor findings).

deterministic_validation.evidence: parse_sdrf validate-sdrf -t ms-proteomics -t human -t cell-lines --use_ols_cache_only (under flock) exited 0 with only cell-line-name ontology warnings. sdrf-tools check --offline: CLEAN, exit 0. sdrf-tools structure: OK, exit 0. sdrf-tools score: 99/100, exit 0; it notes only that the recommended characteristics[ancestry category] is missing.

findings.message: 'not applicable' asserts the concept does not apply, but each cell line derives from a distinct, unidentified donor.
findings.evidence: SAMPLE-GUIDELINES: not available = unknown; not applicable = not relevant. 402-91 and TC-71 come from different donors.
findings.correction: Use 'not available', or use per-line donor identifiers such as the Cellosaurus accessions.

findings.location: file (ancestry category, ms2 mass analyzer, collision energy)
findings.message: Recommended or optional technical and sample columns supported by the evidence are absent.
findings.evidence: The RAW headers and PRIDE protocol give CID 30% (MS2 in the ion trap) and HCD 55% (MS3 in the Orbitrap). sdrf-tools score flags the missing recommended characteristics[ancestry category].
findings.correction: Optionally add characteristics[ancestry category] = not available, comment[collision energy] and comment[ms2 mass analyzer].

findings.message: The manifest quotes the RAW sample names as 'F01…F10', but the headers read 'F016'…'F106'.
findings.evidence: raw_header_check.json: Lumos_210702_13 has '4231 TMTpro F016' and Lumos_210702_22 has '4231 TMTpro F106'. The fraction ordering is still consistent.
findings.correction: Quote the exact header strings in the manifest. No SDRF change is needed.
